prerequisiteReasons.pgvector: Explains the in-database vector storage and similarity search that pgai composes.
prerequisiteReasons.pgai-vectorizer: Explains the managed pipeline that keeps source rows and embeddings synchronized.
prerequisiteReasons.llm-from-sql: Explains the SQL-callable model operations that complete pgai's in-database workflow.

relations.reason: RAG is a major application assembled from pgai's capabilities, not required background for understanding the suite's composition.

prerequisiteReasons.sql: Explains the query expressions and functions through which the model calls are composed.
prerequisiteReasons.embedding: Explains the vector output returned by SQL-callable embedding functions.

relations.reason: RAG is one workflow assembled from SQL model calls and retrieval, not required theory for understanding model functions in SQL.
Both learn shared prior structure from data, but empirical Bayes plugs in estimated hyperparameters while hierarchical Bayes retains them as uncertain variables in the joint posterior.

prerequisiteReasons.transaction: Defines the atomicity and durability promises that WAL implements across a crash.
prerequisiteReasons.page-cache: Explains why changed data can remain only in volatile memory at commit time.
prerequisiteReasons.writeback: Explains deferred page flushing and the force-to-stable-storage operation used for the log at commit.

relations.reason: The sequential-log-versus-scattered-page performance explanation uses the block layer's I/O cost model, but that model is not required to understand WAL's durability and recovery mechanism.

prerequisiteReasons.binary-search-tree: Establishes why an ordered branching structure can avoid a linear table scan.
prerequisiteReasons.key-value: Defines the value-to-row-location mapping stored by an index entry.
prerequisiteReasons.b-tree: Explains the shallow, disk-oriented ordered structure used by range-capable indexes.

relations.reason: An index is a secondary value-to-row-location structure inside a relational database; a key-value store is a primary database architecture with durable, networked, key-only access.

prerequisiteReasons.binary-search-tree: Establishes the ordered branching search mechanism that a B-tree generalizes to high fan-out.

relations.reason: A production B-tree sizes a node to a fixed storage page; this substrate detail enriches the fan-out explanation but is not required to understand the search-tree mechanism.
The block layer's per-I/O cost model explains why high fan-out is valuable on storage, but a learner can understand the B-tree mechanism without first learning OS I/O internals.

softmax.objective: Turn scores into normalized weights and explain why shifting every score preserves them.

prerequisiteReasons.exponential-function: Exponentiating each score produces positive weights.
prerequisiteReasons.arithmetic: Dividing by the sum normalizes the weights.
prerequisiteReasons.probability-distribution: The resulting weights are nonnegative and sum to one.

online-softmax.objective: Update a stable softmax normalizer when a new block changes the maximum.

prerequisiteReasons.softmax: The streaming recurrence preserves the same softmax denominator.

relations.reason: The running normalizer can be fused with a weighted value accumulator to stream attention tiles.

transformer-attention.objective: Explain how query-key scores select a weighted combination of value vectors.

prerequisiteReasons.softmax: Each score row becomes normalized weights over values.
prerequisiteReasons.vector-dot-product: A query-key dot product provides a compatibility score.
prerequisiteReasons.matrix-multiplication: Matrix products compute all scores and weighted outputs efficiently.

flash-attention.objective: Explain why tiling and online normalization avoid storing the full attention matrix.

prerequisiteReasons.transformer-attention: Defines the attention computation whose result the tiled algorithm preserves.
prerequisiteReasons.online-softmax: Explains how partial normalizers and weighted outputs combine across tiles.
